value: soft topologies - a topology-like structure on the collection of all soft sets over a fixed set of alternatives - together with the general procedures that generate them from crisp topologies or from bases for topologies

how to construct soft topologies from standard (crisp) topologies or their bases, what a soft counterpart of topological separability should be, and when the generated soft topology is soft second-countable

extends the known topology-to-soft-topology construction to a family of topologies and to a family of bases (one per attribute), proposes two soft-separability notions, characterises soft second-countability, and exhibits the first non-trivial soft second-countable soft topologies

quote: This section introduces a novel procedure for the construction of soft topologies. It builds on the concept of a base for a crisp topology. We investigate some fundamental properties of this mechanism.

Second-countable crisp topologies are those that have countable bases. It is straightforward to extend the concept to soft topologies: remember that a soft topology with a countable soft base is a soft second-countable or S2C soft topology. This concept is superfluous when both X and E are finite because in this case, all soft topologies are finite (i.e., formed by a finite number of soft sets) thus countable; and countable soft topologies are obviously S2C. In this section we avail ourselves of the ideas in Section 5.1 in order to produce the first non-trivial soft second-countable soft topologies in the literature.

value: for a countable attribute set, the soft topology generated by a family of crisp topologies is soft second-countable if and only if each attribute topology is second-countable
quote: Suppose that 𝛴 = { 𝛴 𝑒 } 𝑒 ∈ 𝐸 is a family of topologies on X, and E is a countable set of attributes. Then 𝜏 ( 𝛴 ) is a S2C soft topology on X if and only if 𝛴 𝑒 is second-countable for each 𝑒 ∈ 𝐸 .
